images.title: After nine thousand
images.purpose: Show that adding one more thousand to 9,000 makes 10 thousands, which is one ten thousand.
images.composition: Ten 1,000 tokens on the left, an arrow in the middle, one 10,000 token on the right and the sum written large underneath.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Left: a group of 10 identical green #009E73 rounded-rectangle tokens in 2 rows of 5, each about 150 by 90 px with a thin dark outline and the label 1,000 in white bold numerals (50 px), 15 px apart. Centre: 1 thick dark arrow pointing right, about 150 px long. Right: 1 larger reddish purple #CC79A7 rounded-rectangle token, about 230 by 150 px, with a thin dark outline and the label 10,000 in dark #1F2937 bold numerals (70 px). Under the green group the caption 10 Thousands, under the purple token the caption Ten Thousand, both in dark sans-serif (36 px). Across the bottom centre one line of large bold dark text, 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000 (80 px), the largest text in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Ten thousands make one ten thousand, so 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000.
images.description: Ten green tokens marked 1,000 in two rows of five, an arrow, and one purple token marked 10,000, with 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000 written below.
images.context: Concept image for What comes after nine thousand? It follows the figure in your maths book (ten 1,000 tokens leading to one 10,000 token) and writes the sum the concept teaches. The video's own example, from 4,150 to 10,150, is told in words and numbers on screen.
images.teaching_notes: Count the tokens aloud: 9 thousands, then one more thousand makes 10 thousands. The token colours are used for every token picture in the chapter: 10,000 purple, 1,000 green, 100 amber, 10 blue, 1 vermilion.

image_decisions.why: The ten 1,000 tokens leading to one 10,000 token make the jump from 9,000 to ten thousand visible.
